Let me analyze this task. I need to estimate software development effort for a specification that describes Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) and Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) related user stories. The user stories U1-U8 describe:

- U1: Investigate include/exclude of message bus/binding jars; decide binding selection and fallback mechanism
- U2: Dependency resolution support when modules use different jar versions
- U3: Publish s-c-d image to DockerHub (CI/CD pipeline for incremental pushes)
- U4: Create a public screencast of "firehose | counter" pipe demo
- U5: Implement undeploy operation for singlenode (single JVM) target
- U6: Add profiles support to core Admin application (e.g., local profile with in-memory strategy)
- U7: Brainstorm and design foundation to port XD modules as s-c-s modules
- U8: Expose counter (metrics) endpoints for dashboards

This is early-stage Spring Cloud Data Flow development (circa 2015 based on the PR reference and XD migration context).

Estimates should be realistic for an experienced developer familiar with Spring ecosystem. Let me estimate:

U1: Investigate binding jar inclusion/exclusion — this is investigation/spike + design decision. ~3-4 days
- Spike on classloading/Maven resolution of binder jars: 2 days
- Design doc for binding selection and fallback: 1 day
- Prototype validation: 1 day
Total U1: ~4 days

U2: Dependency resolution support — resolve conflicting versions at runtime. This is complex. ~8 days
- Design resolution strategy: 2 days
- Implement dependency resolution (Maven Aether-based or module resolver): 4 days
- Tests: 2 days
Total U2: ~8 days

U3: DockerHub publishing — CI pipeline, Dockerfile. ~2-3 days
- Dockerfile + image build: 1 day
- CI integration for incremental push: 1 day
- Verification/docs: 0.5-1 day
Total U3: ~3 days

U4: Screencast creation — prepare demo, script, record, edit, publish. ~2 days

- Design undeploy strategy (jobs + streams): 1 day
- Implement SPI changes + controller/REST endpoint: 2 days
- Singlenode deployer undeploy implementation: 1.5 days
- Tests: 1.5 days

- Design repository strategy interface + profile config: 1 day
- Implement in-memory repository + profile wiring: 2 days

Cross-cutting:

technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline stack: Java 17+, Spring Framework 6.x / Spring Boot 3.x, Maven multi-module build, JUnit 5 and AssertJ for tests.

U1/U2: Binder (message bus binding) jars are treated as optional runtime dependencies resolved from a Maven repository using Eclipse Aether (Maven Resolver); each binder is loaded in an isolated child-first classloader so conflicting transitive versions (e.g., different spring-data versions) do not collide.

U1: Binding selection order is: explicit deployment property > single binder found on classpath/resolution result > fallback to a default binder; if no binder is resolvable, deployment fails fast with a descriptive error.
U2: A dedicated module-resolver component computes a resolved, de-conflicted artifact graph per module at deployment time, with highest-version-wins plus explicit override properties.

U5: Undeploy is added to the Deployer SPI as an idempotent operation with a single consistent strategy for both jobs and streams; the singlenode (single JVM) deployer implementation stops and deregisters the in-process module instances; a REST endpoint on the Admin app triggers undeploy.

U6: Repository backends are selected via Spring Profiles; the 'local' profile wires an in-memory, ConcurrentHashMap-backed stream repository; the repository abstraction is interface-based so persistent backends can be added later.

U7: XD modules are ported by wrapping existing module logic as Spring Cloud Stream functional modules (source/processor/sink) with auto-configuration; the design is captured in an architecture document plus one proof-of-concept ported module.
U8: Counter metrics are exposed via REST endpoints on the Admin app backed by a pluggable counter repository service; payload format supports dashboard consumption for the firehose | counter demo.
U3: A Dockerfile-based image for s-c-d is built and pushed to DockerHub by CI on every merge to the main branch, tagged with latest and the commit SHA.
U4: The screencast is scripted around the firehose | counter pipe, recorded with screen-capture tooling, lightly edited, and published publicly (e.g., YouTube).
assumptions: One experienced developer (the author) performs all work; effort is measured in 8-hour workdays and excludes calendar delays such as review wait times.
An existing s-c-d / s-c-s codebase and repository baseline already exists; this increment builds on it rather than starting from scratch.
CI infrastructure (e.g., Jenkins/Concourse/GitHub Actions) and DockerHub account/credentials are already available.
Design details referenced externally (e.g., PR #19 for undeploy) are accessible and do not need to be reverse-engineered.
A firehose (or simulated equivalent) source and a counter sink are available for demo and metrics validation.
Community/code review feedback cycles are brief and their rework is covered within the testing/hardening activities.
Documentation effort is lightweight (READMEs, config samples, and one design document for U7).

activities.activity_description: Set up/verify the Maven multi-module build, Java 17 toolchain, baseline CI job, and developer environment for the s-c-d/s-c-s increment.
Investigate how message bus/binding jars can be included or excluded (classpath layout, classloading options, resolution sources) to inform binding selection and fallback.

activities.activity_name: U1: Binding selection and fallback design + prototype
activities.activity_description: Define the binding selection order and no-binding fallback mechanism; validate with a small prototype exercising binder isolation.
Design the Aether-based resolution strategy for handling conflicting jar versions across modules, including override properties and resolution output format.
Implement the module-resolver component that resolves, de-conflicts, and stages the correct artifacts for module deployment at runtime.
Unit and integration tests covering version-conflict scenarios (e.g., two direct-bind modules with different spring-data versions), overrides, and failure modes.
Analyze the existing XD module model (types, options, packaging, lifecycle) and catalog what must be preserved when porting to s-c-s modules.
Brainstorm and document the foundation for porting XD modules to s-c-s (module contract, auto-configuration approach, migration guide outline) and validate with one proof-of-concept ported module.
Design the repository abstraction and how Spring Profiles select the backend strategy in the core Admin application.

activities.activity_name: U6: In-memory repository and local profile implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement the in-memory stream repository and wire it to the 'local' profile; ensure Admin configuration activates the strategy per profile.

activities.activity_name: U6: Profile tests and configuration docs
activities.activity_description: Tests for profile activation and in-memory repository behavior, plus configuration documentation for selecting backends via profiles.
Determine a consistent undeploy strategy for both jobs and streams (prerequisite from PR #19), including idempotency and error semantics.

activities.activity_name: U5: Undeploy SPI and Admin REST endpoint
activities.activity_description: Extend the Deployer SPI with undeploy and expose it through the Admin application's controller/REST layer.
Implement undeploy in the singlenode (single JVM) deployer: stop running stream/job module instances, release resources, and deregister them.
Unit and integration tests for undeploying running streams and jobs on the singlenode target, including repeated/failed undeploy edge cases.

activities.activity_name: U8: Counter metrics endpoint contract design
activities.activity_description: Define the REST contract (paths, payload format, query options) for exposing counter metrics suitable for dashboard consumption.

activities.activity_name: U8: Counter service and REST endpoints implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement the counter metrics service backed by a pluggable repository and the Admin REST endpoints exposing counter values.

activities.activity_name: U8: Counter endpoint tests and dashboard validation
activities.activity_description: Tests for the counter endpoints and validation that a dashboard can consume them for the firehose | counter pipe.

activities.activity_name: U3: s-c-d Dockerfile and local image build
activities.activity_description: Author the Dockerfile for the s-c-d image and validate building and running it locally.

activities.activity_name: U3: CI pipeline for incremental DockerHub push
activities.activity_description: Configure the CI pipeline to build the image and push to DockerHub on each merged commit, with latest and commit-SHA tags and credential handling.
Verify end-to-end automated publishing to DockerHub and document the image naming, tagging, and usage.

activities.activity_name: U4: Demo environment and screencast script
activities.activity_description: Prepare the firehose | counter demo environment and write the screencast script showcasing s-c-s and the development experience.

activities.activity_name: U4: Record, edit, and publish screencast
activities.activity_description: Record the screencast, perform light editing/captioning, and publish it publicly.
Cross-feature integration testing (deploy/undeploy with binder resolution, profiles, metrics endpoints, container image), bug fixing, and hardening.
Consolidate README/config documentation and write release notes covering U1-U8 deliverables.
